facts.statement: Draconyx is a genus of ornithopod dinosaur that lived in the Late Jurassic in what is now Portugal.
facts.quote: Draconyx (meaning "dragon claw") is a genus of ornithopod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of what is now Portugal.

facts.statement: The fossil was found in the Lourinhã Formation in 1991 and described by Octávio Mateus and Miguel Telles Antunes in 2001.
facts.quote: It was found in the Lourinhã Formation in 1991, and described by Octávio Mateus and Miguel Telles Antunes in 2001.

facts.statement: The species name loureiroi honors João de Loureiro, a Portuguese Jesuit priest and pioneer in Portuguese paleontology.
facts.quote: The specific name is in honour of João de Loureiro, a Portuguese jesuit priest, a pioneer in Portuguese palaeontology.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen ML 357 is a partial skeleton lacking the skull, consisting of various limb bones, vertebrae, and teeth.
facts.quote: The holotype, ML 357, a partial skeleton lacking the skull, consists of two maxillary teeth, three caudal centra, one chevron, a distal epiphysis of right humerus, one manual phalanx, three manual unguals, a distal epiphysis of the right femur, the proximal and distal epiphyses of the tibia and fibula, an astragalus, a calcanaeum, three tarsals, four metatarsals and pedal phalanges.

facts.statement: The holotype was found in 1991 at Vale de Frades by Carlos Anunciação in layers dating to the Tithonian.
facts.quote: It was in 1991 found at Vale de Frades by Carlos Anunciação of the Museu da Lourinhã, in layers of the Bombarral Unit dating to the Tithonian.

facts.statement: Histological analysis indicates the holotype specimen reached skeletal maturity between 27 and 31 years of age.
facts.quote: Histology shows that the holotype specimen reached skeletally maturity after the age between 27 and 31 years old.

facts.statement: Draconyx was a small bipedal herbivore.
facts.quote: Draconyx was a small bipedal herbivore.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Draconyx to be 3.5 meters long and weigh 150 kilograms in 2010.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul in 2010 estimated the length at 3.5 metres, the weight at 150 kilograms.

facts.statement: Mateus and Antunes classified Draconyx as a member of Iguanodontia and specifically Camptosauridae based on features of the teeth and femur.
facts.quote: According to Mateus and Antunes (2001), Draconyx loureiroi is a member of the Iguanodontia, more specifically the Camptosauridae, based on the maxillary teeth, which have a strong vertical primary ridge on the distal side of the labial crown, and the femur, which is curved and has a prominent lesser trochanter.

facts.statement: A 2022 article places Draconyx within the clade Styracosterna, differing from earlier classifications.
facts.quote: An article in 2022 places Draconyx as a Styracosterna.

facts.statement: Draconyx lived during the Tithonian stage, between 149.2 and 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Tithonian (149.2 to 145.06 million years ago)
